newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Zalm sees need for coordinated labour policies.
newsitem.headline: Zalm sees need for coordinated labour policies.

text.p: Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said on Monday there would be a need for greater coordination of labour policies under monetary union alongside a centralised monetary policy.

"If you have a centralised monetary policy, then I suppose there is a greater need for coordination of labour policy," he told a news conference after a meeting of European Union finance ministers here.

His comments were somewhat different from those made earlier this year when he dismissed French calls for greater coordination of economic policies under monetary union which would play a role alongside the future European Central Bank.

Earlier France's new finance minister, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, refused to back an EU stability pact limiting budget deficits under the euro until there had been further discussions on how to improve coordination of economic and labour policies.
Zalm reiterated that he still hoped to get an agreement on the stability pact before an EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17.
"Everyone is doing all they can, and I mean all member states are doing everything they can to sort it all out as soon as possible," he said.
"Everybody wants the pact to be completed in Amsterdam. I can't guarantee it, we are short on time," he said.
He said the EU could consider a special resolution on growth and employment which would complement the stability pact's insistence on budget discipline.
He said one way of resolving the stability pact dispute in time for Amsterdam would be to hold a special meeting of EU finance ministers before the summit, but said no decision had been made on this.
He declined to say whether the Netherlands might consider holding a special summit after Amsterdam to approve the pact.
"I don't think it is very useful to discuss options which are not first options," he said.

New French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is not due to deliver his keynote policy speech to parliament until June 19, raising speculation that an agreement on the stability pact could only be struck after that.
